subject: Helix: Clarifications on isolated/on-prem deployment operational controls and procurement steps
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@helixhealth.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: procurements@helixhealth.com
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:31:00 -0700
Subject: RFP follow-up: Clarifications on isolated deployment ops

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The procurement team at Helix has a few follow-ups on the isolated / air-gapped deployment profile you described in the RFP response. We're consolidating answers for our security and procurement review. Can you confirm the following items for an on-prem, fully isolated install?

1) Upgrade and patching: what is the offline patch delivery model? Are patches delivered as signed artifacts we can pull into our air-gapped environment? Is there an attestation process we can use to verify patches before applying them?

2) Support & remote troubleshooting: does Redwood require any outbound connectivity for remote support? If remote support is required, what options exist (on-prem console agent vs. VPN/temporary tunnel) and what telemetry is shared?

3) SBOM and third-party components: can you provide a Bill of Materials (SBOM) for the runtime and any embedded libs, and a cadence for updates?

4) Backup / DR: what backup tooling do you recommend for model artifacts and KV cache in an offline deployment? Does Redwood provide tooling or orchestration for scheduled backups/restores?

5) Contract/procurement: do you support purchase orders for on-prem licensing, and is there a standard SOW for installation services? Any lead times we should plan for?

We're on a tight timeline for our security review and aim to finalize vendor selection by May 21. If you can provide written answers and any supporting artifacts, that would be very helpful.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Security & Procurement Liaison
Helix Health Systems

From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: Clarifications on isolated deployment ops (technical answers)

Tessa / team — draft technical responses below that we can include in the consolidated email. I kept answers concise for the customer's security team; happy to expand any section.

1) Upgrade & patching
- Delivery model: we provide signed artifact bundles (tar.gz with accompanying signature) that contain runtime binaries, model runtime bits, and migration scripts. Customers can host these bundles internally and push them to air-gapped clusters via standard change-control processes.
- Attestation: each bundle includes a PGP signature and SHA256 checksums. We also publish a signed manifest and release notes in the artifacts bundle. For higher assurance customers we offer an HSM-signing option as part of a premium support add-on.

2) Support & remote troubleshooting
- Outbound connectivity: Redwood does not require persistent outbound connectivity for the runtime. Remote support options:
  * On-prem console agent (push-based diagnostics) that stores logs locally; customers can export bundles and upload to a secure intake portal.
  * Temporary customer-initiated tunnel: customer opens a short-lived VPN/tunnel to our support subnet; access is limited by IP allowlist and expires after the session.
- Telemetry: by default, no telemetry is sent. If enabled for troubleshooting, telemetry is limited to anonymized runtime metrics and explicit log bundles exported by the customer. We provide a telemetry opt-in and a manifest describing exactly which fields may be included.

3) SBOM and third-party components
- We provide a CycloneDX SBOM (JSON + human-readable PDF) covering primary runtime, language runtimes, and third-party libs. SBOMs are regenerated with each release and included in the signed artifact bundle.

4) Backup / DR
- Model artifacts: we recommend scheduled incremental snapshots of model artifact directories to an internal object store (S3-compatible) behind the customer's network. Redwood supplies a small orchestration utility (offline-capable) to validate checksums and coordinate retention.
- KV cache & state: we support scheduled cold-backup exports of KV checkpoints (protobuf files) plus a restore utility. For mission-critical setups we recommend multi-site backups and periodic restore drills.

5) Contract / procurement notes
- PO support: yes. Standard on-prem license + install SOW. Typical install SOW covers: on-site kickoff (remote option), artifact handoff, runbook workthrough, and one week of hypercare. Lead time: 2–3 weeks post-PO for standard installs; custom timelines for large multi-site projects.

Attachments we can provide: SBOM, runbook checklist, a sample network diagram and an example install SOW.

Let me know if you want me to redact internal tool names from the SBOM.

—Markus
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Appended are concise answers and the requested artifacts for your security and procurement review. See attachments: redwood-sbom-latest.pdf, onprem-maintenance-runbook.xlsx, network-segmentation-diagram.png.

Summary (high level):
- Patching: signed, checksummed bundles included with manifest and optional HSM signing.
- Remote support: customer-initiated tunnels or exportable diagnostic bundles; no persistent outbound telemetry by default.
- SBOM: CycloneDX SBOM provided in the artifact bundle; regenerated with each release.
- Backup/DR: offline utilities for incremental model snapshotting and KV checkpoint exports; recommended restore drills for DR verification.
- Procurement: PO accepted; standard SOW includes kickoff + one week hypercare; typical lead time 2–3 weeks.

If acceptable, Vanessa will follow up with our commercial docs (SOW template + PO instructions). Also attaching a sample network diagram to show recommended segmentation for an isolated cluster.

We can also schedule a short technical call with Markus to walk through the SBOM and the upgrade signing flow if your security team prefers a live walkthrough.

Thanks — looking forward to your feedback.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference
